tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,

32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts

1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

schema.name: Agent
schema.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

1	# Module migration brief (read fully before editing)
2	
3	Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). We are migrating from Stylus SDK 0.9.0 +
4	motsu test framework to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 + the SDK's own testing framework (`stylus-test`,
5	exposed as `stylus_sdk::testing::*`, i.e. `TestVM`), on Rust 1.91.0 stable.
6	
7	Your worktree is the path given in your task. It is based on git commit 7e36233, which
8	already moved the manifests and the shared core (utils/address, utils/storage_slot,
9	proxy/erc1967/utils, utils/cryptography/eip712) to the new API. The crate does not
10	compile yet: other agents own the other modules and are fixing them in parallel.
11	
12	Read first:
13	- /tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md : the API decisions. Follow them exactly.
14	- The SDK source (read-only reference, do NOT build or run anything inside it):
15	  /tmp/bench/downloads/stylus-sdk-rs-0.10.10 . Useful paths: stylus-core/src/host.rs (VM
16	  accessor traits), stylus-core/src/calls/ (call contexts), stylus-sdk/src/call/ (call
17	  functions), stylus-test/README.md (TestVM usage), examples/ (SDK example contracts).
18	
19	## Ownership
20	Edit ONLY the files in your ownership list (given in your task). If you need a change in
21	a file you do not own, do not make it: list it under "requests" in your final report.
22	Never change a public item's name. Signature changes are allowed only as in api-map.md
23	or when needed to remove a global accessor (then document it in your report).
24	
25	## What "done" means for your files
26	1. Non-test code compiles on SDK 0.10.10 with NO global accessors: no `msg::`, `evm::`,
27	   `block::`, `contract::` free functions, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error, MethodError, Call,
28	   StaticCallContext}` (use `stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::{Error, MethodError}`;
29	   `Call`/`StaticCallContext` come from `stylus_sdk::prelude::*`). Host access is
30	   `self.vm()` (HostAccess) or the `context` parameter.
31	2. Every `pub trait I...` that is a public interface is tagged `#[public]`, and every
32	   `impl Trait for X` of such a trait is tagged `#[public]`. Traits with associated consts
33	   are NOT `#[public]`. Routed methods must be written in the `#[public] impl` block itself:
34	   default bodies in a `#[public]` trait are not routed.
35	3. Every motsu test is converted to a plain `#[test]` using `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM`:
36	     let vm = TestVM::default();
37	     let mut c = Token::from(&vm);
38	     vm.set_sender(ALICE);            // msg::sender
39	     vm.set_value(U256::from(1));     // msg::value
40	     vm.set_block_timestamp(..); vm.set_chain_id(..); vm.set_balance(addr, v);
41	     vm.get_emitted_logs(); vm.mock_call(..); vm.mock_delegate_call(..); vm.mock_static_call(..)
42	   Use `crate::test_utils::{ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE}` instead of motsu's injected accounts.
43	   motsu's `Contract::<T>::new()` + `.sender(alice)` become `T::from(&vm)` + `vm.set_sender`.
44	   Property tests (proptest inside a test) must build a fresh TestVM per case.
45	4. Preserve every test scenario and every assertion. Do NOT delete, weaken, or merge away a
46	   test unless it is an exact duplicate of another test in the same file (then say so).
47	   Keep `#[should_panic]`/revert checks as revert checks (`is_err()` / matching the error).
48	5. Do NOT change storage layout: field order and field types of every `#[storage]`
49	   struct stay byte-for-byte the same. (Proxies depend on it.)
50	6. Preserve the public ABI: function names, selectors, parameter and return types, error
51	   types and their encodings. Preserve behavior. Only the Rust-level API for host access
52	   may change (documented in the report).
53	7. Rustdoc stays accurate: where the call pattern changed (context/self.vm()), update the
54	   doc text. No commented-out code, no TODO left for things you were asked to do.
55	8. `#[cfg(test)]` modules use `use super::*;` and explicit imports as the rest of the repo.
56	
57	## Verification (use the 1.91.0 toolchain; never use nightly for building)
58	- Check your files only:
59	    cd <worktree> && cargo +1.91.0 check -p openzeppelin-stylus > /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log 2>&1
60	    grep -A1 '^error' /tmp/bench/logs/<you>-check.log | grep -- '--> ' | sed 's/.*--> //' | sort | uniq -c
61	  Only errors in YOUR files matter until the whole crate compiles.
62	- Tests: `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib <filter>` runs only once the whole
63	  test target compiles. Until then, check your test code with
64	  `cargo +1.91.0 test -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib --no-run` and filter errors to your files.
65	- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>` (the repo's
66	  rustfmt.toml uses options only nightly rustfmt supports). Run it on your files at the end.
67	- Clippy (once the crate compiles): `cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p openzeppelin-stylus --all-targets -- -D warnings`
68	  Lints are pedantic (see workspace Cargo.toml). Fix warnings in your files.
69	
70	## Git
71	- Work and commit on your branch (already created for your worktree). Small logical commits,
72	  message style: `refactor(<area>): <what>` or `test(<area>): <what>`. Each message ends with:
73	    Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
74	- Commit only your files. Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not run `git reset --hard`
75	  or any command that touches other worktrees.
76	
77	## Final report (your last message, at most 40 lines)
78	- Files changed; commit list (`git log --oneline 7e36233..HEAD`).
79	- Signature changes (name: old -> new).
80	- Test inventory: number of test functions before (`git show 7e36233:<file> | grep -cE '#\[(motsu::)?test\]'`)
81	  and after, per file; any test you merged or removed (with reason).
82	- Compile status of your files (lib / tests); whether the crate compiled as a whole at the time.
83	- Requests to other owners; blockers; anything you were unsure about.

1	# SDK 0.9.0 -> 0.10.10 API map (decisions for this migration)
2	
3	Accessors (global -> VM):
4	  msg::sender()        -> self.vm().msg_sender()          (MessageAccess)
5	  msg::value()         -> self.vm().msg_value()           (MessageAccess)
6	  contract::address()  -> self.vm().contract_address()    (AccountAccess)
7	  contract::balance(a) -> self.vm().balance(a)            (AccountAccess)
8	  block::timestamp()   -> self.vm().block_timestamp()     (BlockAccess)
9	  block::chainid()     -> self.vm().chain_id()            (ChainAccess)
10	  evm::log(E{..})      -> self.vm().log(E{..})            (LogAccess)
11	Free functions that need the host take `context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>` (or
12	`&mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>)` when they also build a call context).
13	
14	Calls (stylus_sdk::call takes the host explicitly):
15	  call::static_call(Call::new(), t, d)       -> call::static_call(self.vm(), Call::new(), t, d)
16	  Call::new_in(self)                         -> Call::new_mutating(self)  (bind to a local first:
17	                                                the borrow of self must end before self.vm())
18	  Call::new_in(self).value(v)                -> Call::new_payable(self, v)
19	  unsafe call::delegate_call(ctx, t, d)      -> unsafe { call::delegate_call(self.vm(), ctx, t, d) }
20	  sol_interface methods: f(ctx, args)        -> f(self.vm(), ctx, args)
21	Import paths:
22	  stylus_sdk::call::{MethodError}            -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError
23	  stylus_sdk::call::Error                    -> stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error
24	  stylus_sdk::call::{Call, StaticCallContext}-> in prelude (stylus_sdk::prelude::*)
25	  stylus_sdk::evm / msg / block / contract   -> removed (use self.vm())
26	
27	Traits:
28	  Every public interface trait (`pub trait I...` routed by `#[public]`) must itself carry
29	  `#[public]`, and every `impl Trait for X` of such a trait must carry `#[public]`.
30	  `#[public]` traits may not contain associated consts (e.g. IEip712), keep those plain.
31	  Default bodies in `#[public]` traits are NOT routed: the router is generated from the impl
32	  block's items, so every routed method must be written in the `#[public] impl`.
33	
34	Storage slots (SDK 0.10 custom slot pattern):
35	  StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(slot)  -> StorageSlot::get_slot::<ST>(context, slot)
36	      internally: unsafe { ST::new(slot, offset, context.vm().clone()) }
37	
38	Decisions taken while fixing the shared core (apply everywhere):
39	  AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(context: &mut (impl TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM>), target, data)
40	      builds `let call = Call::new_mutating(context);` FIRST, then `call::delegate_call(context.vm(), call, ...)`.
41	  AddressUtils::verify_call_result_from_target(context: &impl HostAccess<Host = VM>, target, result)
42	  AddressUtils::has_code(context, addr) -> bool          (pub(crate); replaces Address::has_code())
43	  Erc1967Utils: every fn that reads/writes a slot or emits/gets msg value takes `context` first:
44	      get_implementation(context), get_admin(context), change_admin(context, new_admin),
45	      get_beacon(context), upgrade_to_and_call(context, impl, data), upgrade_beacon_to_and_call(context, beacon, data)
46	  IEip712: `pub trait IEip712: HostAccess` (no #[public], it has associated consts);
47	      chain_id(&self), contract_address(&self) are methods, not associated fns.
48	  Interface wrappers from sol_interface!: f(context.vm(), Call::new()/Call::new_mutating(self)/..., args).
49	      Static calls use Call::new() (no storage borrow needed).
50	Test fixtures: contracts/src/test_utils.rs exports ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE (const Address).

1	//! Implementation of the [`UpgradeableBeacon`] contract.
2	
3	use alloc::{vec, vec::Vec};
4	
5	use alloy_primitives::Address;
6	pub use sol::*;
7	use stylus_sdk::{stylus_core::calls::errors::MethodError, prelude::*, storage::StorageAddress};
8	
9	use crate::{
10	    access::ownable::{self, IOwnable, Ownable},
11	    proxy::beacon::IBeacon};
12	
13	#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
14	mod sol {
15	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
16	
17	    sol! {
18	        /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `implementation`
19	        /// of the beacon is invalid.
20	        ///
21	        /// * `implementation` - Address of the invalid implementation.
22	        #[derive(Debug)]
23	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
24	        error BeaconInvalidImplementation(address implementation);
25	
26	        /// Emitted when the implementation returned by the beacon is changed.
27	        #[derive(Debug)]
28	        #[allow(missing_docs)]
29	        event Upgraded(address indexed implementation);
30	    }
31	}
32	
33	/// An [`UpgradeableBeacon`] error.
34	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
35	pub enum Error {
36	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `implementation`
37	    /// of the beacon is invalid.
38	    InvalidImplementation(BeaconInvalidImplementation),
39	    /// The caller account is not authorized to perform an operation.
40	    UnauthorizedAccount(ownable::OwnableUnauthorizedAccount),
41	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `owner` of the
42	    /// beacon is invalid.
43	    InvalidOwner(ownable::OwnableInvalidOwner)}
44	
45	impl MethodError for Error {
46	    fn encode(self) -> alloc::vec::Vec<u8> {
47	        self.into()
48	    }
49	}
50	
51	impl From<ownable::Error> for Error {
52	    fn from(err: ownable::Error) -> Self {
53	        match err {
54	            ownable::Error::UnauthorizedAccount(err) => {
55	                Error::UnauthorizedAccount(err)
56	            }
57	            ownable::Error::InvalidOwner(err) => Error::InvalidOwner(err)}
58	    }
59	}
60	
61	/// This contract is used in conjunction with one or more instances of
62	/// [`BeaconProxy`][BeaconProxy] to determine their implementation contract,
63	/// which is where they will delegate all function calls.
64	///
65	/// An owner is able to change the implementation the beacon points to, thus
66	/// upgrading the proxies that use this beacon.
67	///
68	/// [BeaconProxy]: super::BeaconProxy
69	#[public]
70	pub trait IUpgradeableBeacon: IBeacon + IOwnable {
71	    /// Upgrades the beacon to a new implementation.
72	    ///
73	    /// # Arguments
74	    ///
75	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
76	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
77	    ///
78	    /// # Errors
79	    ///
80	    /// Implementing contracts should define their own error types for this
81	    /// function. Typically, errors may include:
82	    /// * The caller is not authorized to perform the upgrade.
83	    /// * The new implementation address is invalid (e.g., not a contract).
84	    /// * The upgrade operation failed for contract-specific reasons.
85	    ///
86	    /// The error should be encoded as a [`Vec<u8>`].
87	    fn upgrade_to(
88	        &mut self,
89	        new_implementation: Address,
90	    ) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
91	}
92	
93	/// State of an [`UpgradeableBeacon`] contract.
94	#[storage]
95	pub struct UpgradeableBeacon {
96	    /// The address of the implementation contract.
97	    implementation: StorageAddress,
98	    /// The [`Ownable`] contract that owns the beacon.
99	    ownable: Ownable}
100	
101	unsafe impl TopLevelStorage for UpgradeableBeacon {}
102	
103	#[public]
104	#[implements(IBeacon, IOwnable)]
105	impl UpgradeableBeacon {
106	    /// Sets the address of the initial implementation, and the initial owner
107	    /// who can upgrade the beacon.
108	    ///
109	    /// # Arguments
110	    ///
111	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
112	    /// * `implementation` - The address of the initial implementation.
113	    ///
114	    /// # Errors
115	    ///
116	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If `implementation` is not a
117	    ///   contract.
118	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedAccount`] - If the caller is not the owner.
119	    ///
120	    /// # Events
121	    ///
122	    /// * [`Upgraded`].
123	    #[constructor]
124	    pub fn constructor(
125	        &mut self,
126	        implementation: Address,
127	        initial_owner: Address,
128	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
129	        self.ownable.constructor(initial_owner)?;
130	        self.set_implementation(implementation)?;
131	        Ok(())
132	    }
133	
134	    /// Upgrades the beacon to a new implementation.
135	    ///
136	    /// # Arguments
137	    ///
138	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
139	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
140	    ///
141	    /// # Errors
142	    ///
143	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If `new_implementation` is not a
144	    ///   contract.
145	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedAccount`] - If the caller is not the owner.
146	    ///
147	    /// # Events
148	    ///
149	    /// * [`Upgraded`].
150	    pub fn upgrade_to(
151	        &mut self,
152	        new_implementation: Address,
153	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
154	        self.ownable.only_owner()?;
155	        self.set_implementation(new_implementation)
156	    }
157	
158	    /// Upgrades the beacon to a new implementation.
159	    ///
160	    /// # Arguments
161	    ///
162	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
163	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
164	    ///
165	    /// # Errors
166	    ///
167	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If `new_implementation` is not a
168	    ///   contract.
169	    ///
170	    /// # Events
171	    ///
172	    /// * [`Upgraded`].
173	    fn set_implementation(
174	        &mut self,
175	        new_implementation: Address,
176	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
177	        if !new_implementation.has_code() {
178	            return Err(Error::InvalidImplementation(
179	                BeaconInvalidImplementation {
180	                    implementation: new_implementation},
181	            ));
182	        }
183	        self.implementation.set(new_implementation);
184	        self.vm().log(Upgraded { implementation: new_implementation });
185	        Ok(())
186	    }
187	}
188	
189	#[public]
190	impl IBeacon for UpgradeableBeacon {
191	    fn implementation(&self) -> Result<Address, Vec<u8>> {
192	        Ok(self.implementation.get())
193	    }
194	}
195	
196	#[public]
197	impl IOwnable for UpgradeableBeacon {

200	    }

202	    fn transfer_ownership(

207	    }

47	/// A sentinel storage slot used by the implementation to distinguish
48	/// implementation vs. proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]) execution
49	/// contexts.
50	///
51	/// The slot key is derived from `keccak256("Stylus.uups.logic.flag") - 1`,
52	/// chosen to avoid storage collisions with application state.
53	///
54	/// Behavior:
55	/// - When called directly on the implementation, `logic_flag == true`.
56	/// - When called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]), `logic_flag ==
57	///   false` (i.e., the proxy’s storage does not contain this
58	///   implementation-only flag).
59	///
60	/// Security notes:
61	/// - This boolean flag replaces Solidity’s `immutable __self` pattern.
62	///
63	/// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
64	pub const LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT: B256 = {
65	    const HASH: [u8; 32] = keccak_const::Keccak256::new()
66	        .update(b"Stylus.uups.logic.flag")
67	        .finalize();
68	    let slot = U256::from_be_bytes(HASH)
69	        .wrapping_sub(uint!(1_U256))
70	        .to_be_bytes::<32>();
71	
72	    B256::new(slot)
73	};

110	/// An [`UUPSUpgradeable`] error.
111	#[derive(SolidityError, Debug)]
112	pub enum Error {
113	    /// The call is from an unauthorized context.
114	    UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext),
115	    /// The storage `slot` is unsupported as a UUID.
116	    UnsupportedProxiableUUID(UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID),
117	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `implementation`
118	    /// of the proxy is invalid.
119	    InvalidImplementation(ERC1967InvalidImplementation),
120	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `admin` of the
121	    /// proxy is invalid.
122	    InvalidAdmin(ERC1967InvalidAdmin),
123	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the `beacon`
124	    /// of the proxy is invalid.
125	    InvalidBeacon(ERC1967InvalidBeacon),
126	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that an upgrade function
127	    /// sees [`stylus_sdk::self.vm().msg_value()`] > [`alloy_primitives::U256::ZERO`]
128	    /// that may be lost.
129	    NonPayable(ERC1967NonPayable),
130	    /// There's no code at `target` (it is not a contract).
131	    EmptyCode(address::AddressEmptyCode),
132	    /// A call to an address target failed. The target may have reverted.
133	    FailedCall(address::FailedCall),
134	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the
135	    /// [`stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call`] failed.
136	    FailedCallWithReason(address::FailedCallWithReason),
137	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the contract is already
138	    /// initialized.
139	    InvalidInitialization(InvalidInitialization),
140	    /// Indicates an error related to the fact that the version is not greater
141	    /// than the current version.
142	    InvalidVersion(InvalidVersion)}

144	impl From<erc1967::utils::Error> for Error {
145	    fn from(e: erc1967::utils::Error) -> Self {
146	        match e {
147	            erc1967::utils::Error::InvalidImplementation(e) => {
148	                Error::InvalidImplementation(e)
149	            }
150	            erc1967::utils::Error::InvalidAdmin(e) => Error::InvalidAdmin(e),
151	            erc1967::utils::Error::InvalidBeacon(e) => Error::InvalidBeacon(e),
152	            erc1967::utils::Error::NonPayable(e) => Error::NonPayable(e),
153	            erc1967::utils::Error::EmptyCode(e) => Error::EmptyCode(e),
154	            erc1967::utils::Error::FailedCall(e) => Error::FailedCall(e),
155	            erc1967::utils::Error::FailedCallWithReason(e) => {
156	                Error::FailedCallWithReason(e)
157	            }
158	        }

173	/// Interface for a UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard) upgradeable
174	/// contract.
175	#[public]
176	pub trait IUUPSUpgradeable: IErc1822Proxiable {
177	    /// Returns the version of the upgrade interface of the contract.
178	    ///
179	    /// NOTE: Make sure to set proper selector in order to make the function
180	    /// compatible with Solidity version.
181	    ///
182	    /// ```rust,ignore
183	    /// #[selector(name = "UPGRADE_INTERFACE_VERSION")]
184	    /// fn upgrade_interface_version(&self) -> String {
185	    ///     self.uups.upgrade_interface_version()
186	    /// }
187	    /// ```
188	    ///
189	    /// # Arguments
190	    ///
191	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
192	    fn upgrade_interface_version(&self) -> String;
193	
194	    /// Upgrade the implementation of the proxy to `new_implementation`, and
195	    /// subsequently execute the function call encoded in `data`.
196	    ///
197	    /// Note: This primitive does not include an authorization mechanism. To
198	    /// restrict who can upgrade, enforce access control in your contract
199	    /// before delegating to this function.
200	    ///
201	    /// # Arguments
202	    ///
203	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
204	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation contract.
205	    /// * `data` - Additional data to be passed to the new implementation.
206	    ///
207	    /// # Errors
208	    ///
209	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If the call is not made through a
210	    ///   valid proxy context.
211	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the new implementation address
212	    ///   is invalid or doesn't implement the required interface.
213	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID`] - If the new implementation
214	    ///   returns an unsupported UUID.
215	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If the upgrade function receives ETH but is
216	    ///   not designed to handle it.
217	    /// * [`Error::EmptyCode`] - If there's no code at the new implementation
218	    ///   address.
219	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] to the
220	    ///   new implementation fails.
221	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the
222	    ///   [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] fails with a specific reason.
223	    ///
224	    /// # Events
225	    ///
226	    /// * [`crate::proxy::erc1967::Upgraded`]: Emitted when the implementation
227	    ///   is upgraded.
228	    ///
229	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
230	    fn upgrade_to_and_call(
231	        &mut self,
232	        new_implementation: Address,
233	        data: Bytes,
234	    ) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>>;
235	}

237	/// A contract that implements the UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard)
238	/// pattern for upgradeable contracts.
239	///
240	/// # Overview
241	///
242	/// This implementation provides upgradeability functionality for proxy
243	/// contracts while maintaining storage compatibility across upgrades. It
244	/// follows the UUPS pattern defined in [EIP-1822], where the upgrade
245	/// logic is included in the implementation contract rather than the proxy.
246	///
247	/// This Stylus version contains some architectural differences compared to
248	/// Solidity's implementation, while maintaining the same security model and
249	/// upgrade flow.
250	///
251	/// # Design Rationale & Differences from Solidity
252	///
253	/// ## Storage-based Context Detection
254	///
255	/// Solidity often relies on an `immutable` self-address to detect context. In
256	/// Stylus, this contract uses a boolean `logic_flag` stored in a dedicated
257	/// slot:
258	/// - When executing directly on the implementation, the constructor has set
259	///   `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage.
260	/// - When executing via proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]), the proxy’s
261	///   storage does not have this flag, so the check reads as `false`.
262	///
263	/// ## Initialization Pattern
264	///
265	/// - Constructor: runs once on implementation deployment, sets `logic_flag`.
266	/// - Runtime initializer: `set_version()` must be invoked via the proxy to
267	///   write this logic’s `VERSION_NUMBER` into the proxy’s storage. This aligns
268	///   the proxy’s version with the logic and enables upgrade paths guarded by
269	///   `only_proxy()`.
270	///
271	/// ## Proxy Safety Checks
272	///
273	/// The [`UUPSUpgradeable::only_proxy`] function ensures that:
274	///
275	/// 1. The call is being made through a `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
276	/// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
277	/// 3. The `VERSION_NUMBER` in implementation equals to the version stored in
278	///    the proxy.
279	///
280	/// **Security Note:** Bypassing these checks could allow unauthorized upgrades
281	/// or break the proxy pattern, potentially leading to storage collisions or
282	/// unauthorized upgrades.
283	///
284	/// # Edge Cases & Pitfalls
285	///
286	/// ## Common Mistakes
287	///
288	/// * The new implementation doesn't expose `set_version()` or the version
289	///   number constant does not increase.
290	/// * Calling upgrade entrypoints directly on the implementation.
291	/// * Using a non-ERC-1967 proxy.
292	/// * Incorrectly implementing `proxiable_uuid()` in derived contracts.
293	///
294	/// ## Security Considerations
295	///
296	/// * Always use the `only_proxy` modifier for upgrade functions
297	/// * Never expose `_upgrade_to_and_call_uups` directly
298	/// * Ensure all storage variables are append-only in upgrades
299	/// * Test upgrades thoroughly on testnet before mainnet deployment
300	///
301	/// # Usage
302	///
303	/// ```rust
304	/// extern crate alloc;
305	///
306	/// use openzeppelin_stylus::proxy::utils::uups_upgradeable::UUPSUpgradeable;
307	/// use stylus_sdk::{prelude::*, storage::StorageU256};
308	///
309	/// #[storage]
310	/// #[entrypoint]
311	/// pub struct MyUpgradeableContract {
312	///     // Must include UUPSUpgradeable as the first field
313	///     uups: UUPSUpgradeable,
314	///
315	///     // Your contract's state variables
316	///     value: StorageU256,
317	///     // ...
318	/// }
319	///
320	/// #[public]
321	/// impl MyUpgradeableContract {
322	///     // Call this via the proxy once to align the proxy's version with the logic.
323	///     pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
324	///         self.uups.set_version().map_err(Into::into)
325	///     }
326	///
327	///     // Your contract's functions
328	/// }
329	/// ```
330	///
331	/// [EIP-1822]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1822
332	/// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
333	/// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
334	#[storage]
335	pub struct UUPSUpgradeable {
336	    /// Logic version number stored in the proxy contract.
337	    pub version: StorageU32}
338	
339	#[public]
340	#[implements(IUUPSUpgradeable, IErc1822Proxiable)]
341	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
342	    /// Initializes implementation-only state used for context checks.
343	    ///
344	    /// Sets `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage to indicate
345	    /// a direct (non-delegated) execution context.
346	    ///
347	    /// # Arguments
348	    ///
349	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
350	    #[constructor]
351	    pub fn constructor(&mut self) {
352	        self.logic_flag().set(true);
353	    }
354	
355	    /// Sets the proxy-stored runtime `version` for this logic
356	    /// (initializer-like).
357	    ///
358	    /// Intended to be called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]) to
359	    /// record `VERSION_NUMBER` in the proxy’s storage.
360	    ///
361	    /// # Arguments
362	    ///
363	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
364	    ///
365	    /// # Errors
366	    ///
367	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If not called via proxy
368	    ///   `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
369	    /// * [`Error::InvalidVersion`] - If the proxy's stored `version` is greater
370	    ///   than this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`.
371	    ///
372	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
373	    pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
374	        if self.not_delegated().is_ok() {
375	            return Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(
376	                UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {},
377	            ));
378	        }
379	        if self.version.get() > VERSION_NUMBER {
380	            return Err(Error::InvalidVersion(InvalidVersion {
381	                current_version: self.version.get().to()}));
382	        }
383	
384	        self.version.set(VERSION_NUMBER);
385	        Ok(())
386	    }
387	}

416	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
417	    /// Get the logic contract version.
418	    ///
419	    /// # Arguments
420	    ///
421	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
422	    #[must_use]
423	    pub fn get_version(&self) -> U32 {
424	        VERSION_NUMBER
425	    }
426	
427	    /// Get the logic flag from the appropriate storage slot.
428	    ///
429	    /// # Arguments
430	    ///
431	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
432	    #[must_use]
433	    pub fn logic_flag(&self) -> StorageBool {
434	        StorageSlot::get_slot::<StorageBool>(LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT)
435	    }
436	
437	    /// Return the value stored in the logic flag slot.
438	    ///
439	    /// # Arguments
440	    ///
441	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
442	    #[must_use]
443	    pub fn is_logic(&self) -> bool {
444	        self.logic_flag().get()
445	    }
446	
447	    /// Ensures the call is being made through a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
448	    ///
449	    /// Checks:
450	    /// 1. Execution is happening via [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] (checked
451	    ///    via `!self.is_logic()`).
452	    /// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy (implementation slot is
453	    ///    non-zero).
454	    /// 3. The proxy state is consistent for this logic (the proxy-stored
455	    ///    version equals this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`).
456	    ///
457	    /// [`onlyProxy`]: https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/c64a1edb67b6e3f4a15cca8909c9482ad33a02b0/contracts/proxy/utils/UUPSUpgradeable.sol#L50
458	    ///
459	    /// # Security Implications
460	    ///
461	    /// This check prevents direct calls to upgrade functions on the
462	    /// implementation contract.
463	    ///
464	    /// Note: This is not a reentrancy guard. Use a dedicated mechanism if
465	    /// reentrancy protection is required.
466	    ///
467	    /// # Edge Cases
468	    ///
469	    /// * Calls from [ERC-1167] minimal proxies are not guaranteed to pass this
470	    ///   check
471	    ///
472	    /// # Arguments
473	    ///
474	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
475	    ///
476	    /// # Errors
477	    ///
478	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If any of the above conditions is
479	    ///   not met
480	    ///
481	    /// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
482	    /// [ERC-1167]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1167
483	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
484	    pub fn only_proxy(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
485	        if self.is_logic()
486	            || Erc1967Utils::get_implementation() == Address::ZERO
487	            || U32::from(self.get_version()) != self.version.get()
488	        {
489	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
490	        } else {
491	            Ok(())
492	        }
493	    }
494	
495	    /// Check that the execution is not being performed through a
496	    /// [`delegate_call`].
497	    ///
498	    /// This allows a function to be callable on the implementing contract
499	    /// but not through proxies.
500	    ///
501	    /// # Arguments
502	    ///
503	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
504	    ///
505	    /// # Errors
506	    ///
507	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If the execution is performed via
508	    ///   [`delegate_call`].
509	    ///
510	    /// [`delegate_call`]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
511	    pub fn not_delegated(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
512	        if self.is_logic() {
513	            Ok(())
514	        } else {
515	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
516	        }
517	    }
518	}

528	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
529	    /// Performs an implementation upgrade with a security check for UUPS
530	    /// proxies, and additional setup call.
531	    ///
532	    /// As a security check, [`IErc1822Proxiable::proxiable_uuid`] is invoked
533	    /// in the new implementation, and the return value is expected to be the
534	    /// implementation slot in ERC-1967.
535	    ///
536	    /// # Arguments
537	    ///
538	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
539	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
540	    /// * `data` - The data to pass to the new implementation.
541	    ///
542	    /// # Errors
543	    ///
544	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the new implementation doesn't
545	    ///   support the required interface or is invalid.
546	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID`] - If the new implementation
547	    ///   returns an unsupported UUID.
548	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If the upgrade function receives ETH but is
549	    ///   not designed to handle it.
550	    /// * [`Error::EmptyCode`] - If there's no code at the new implementation
551	    ///   address.
552	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] to the
553	    ///   new implementation fails.
554	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the
555	    ///   [`stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call`] fails with a specific reason.
556	    ///
557	    /// # Events
558	    ///
559	    /// * [`crate::proxy::erc1967::Erc1967Proxy::Upgraded`]: Emitted when the
560	    ///   implementation is upgraded.
561	    ///
562	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
563	    fn _upgrade_to_and_call_uups(
564	        &mut self,
565	        new_implementation: Address,
566	        data: &Bytes,
567	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
568	        let slot = Erc1822ProxiableInterface::new(new_implementation)
569	            .proxiable_uuid(Call::new_in(self))
570	            .map_err(|_e| {
571	                Error::InvalidImplementation(ERC1967InvalidImplementation {
572	                    implementation: new_implementation})
573	            })?;
574	
575	        if slot == IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT {
576	            Erc1967Utils::upgrade_to_and_call(self, new_implementation, data)
577	                .map_err(Error::from)
578	        } else {
579	            Err(Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID(UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID {
580	                slot}))
581	        }
582	    }
583	}

47	/// A sentinel storage slot used by the implementation to distinguish
48	/// implementation vs. proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]) execution
49	/// contexts.
50	///
51	/// The slot key is derived from `keccak256("Stylus.uups.logic.flag") - 1`,
52	/// chosen to avoid storage collisions with application state.
53	///
54	/// Behavior:
55	/// - When called directly on the implementation, `logic_flag == true`.
56	/// - When called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]), `logic_flag ==
57	///   false` (i.e., the proxy’s storage does not contain this
58	///   implementation-only flag).
59	///
60	/// Security notes:
61	/// - This boolean flag replaces Solidity’s `immutable __self` pattern.
62	///
63	/// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
64	pub const LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT: B256 = {
65	    const HASH: [u8; 32] = keccak_const::Keccak256::new()
66	        .update(b"Stylus.uups.logic.flag")
67	        .finalize();
68	    let slot = U256::from_be_bytes(HASH)
69	        .wrapping_sub(uint!(1_U256))
70	        .to_be_bytes::<32>();
71	
72	    B256::new(slot)
73	};

237	/// A contract that implements the UUPS (Universal Upgradeable Proxy Standard)
238	/// pattern for upgradeable contracts.
239	///
240	/// # Overview
241	///
242	/// This implementation provides upgradeability functionality for proxy
243	/// contracts while maintaining storage compatibility across upgrades. It
244	/// follows the UUPS pattern defined in [EIP-1822], where the upgrade
245	/// logic is included in the implementation contract rather than the proxy.
246	///
247	/// This Stylus version contains some architectural differences compared to
248	/// Solidity's implementation, while maintaining the same security model and
249	/// upgrade flow.
250	///
251	/// # Design Rationale & Differences from Solidity
252	///
253	/// ## Storage-based Context Detection
254	///
255	/// Solidity often relies on an `immutable` self-address to detect context. In
256	/// Stylus, this contract uses a boolean `logic_flag` stored in a dedicated
257	/// slot:
258	/// - When executing directly on the implementation, the constructor has set
259	///   `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage.
260	/// - When executing via proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]), the proxy’s
261	///   storage does not have this flag, so the check reads as `false`.
262	///
263	/// ## Initialization Pattern
264	///
265	/// - Constructor: runs once on implementation deployment, sets `logic_flag`.
266	/// - Runtime initializer: `set_version()` must be invoked via the proxy to
267	///   write this logic’s `VERSION_NUMBER` into the proxy’s storage. This aligns
268	///   the proxy’s version with the logic and enables upgrade paths guarded by
269	///   `only_proxy()`.
270	///
271	/// ## Proxy Safety Checks
272	///
273	/// The [`UUPSUpgradeable::only_proxy`] function ensures that:
274	///
275	/// 1. The call is being made through a `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
276	/// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
277	/// 3. The `VERSION_NUMBER` in implementation equals to the version stored in
278	///    the proxy.
279	///
280	/// **Security Note:** Bypassing these checks could allow unauthorized upgrades
281	/// or break the proxy pattern, potentially leading to storage collisions or
282	/// unauthorized upgrades.
283	///
284	/// # Edge Cases & Pitfalls
285	///
286	/// ## Common Mistakes
287	///
288	/// * The new implementation doesn't expose `set_version()` or the version
289	///   number constant does not increase.
290	/// * Calling upgrade entrypoints directly on the implementation.
291	/// * Using a non-ERC-1967 proxy.
292	/// * Incorrectly implementing `proxiable_uuid()` in derived contracts.
293	///
294	/// ## Security Considerations
295	///
296	/// * Always use the `only_proxy` modifier for upgrade functions
297	/// * Never expose `_upgrade_to_and_call_uups` directly
298	/// * Ensure all storage variables are append-only in upgrades
299	/// * Test upgrades thoroughly on testnet before mainnet deployment
300	///
301	/// # Usage
302	///
303	/// ```rust
304	/// extern crate alloc;
305	///
306	/// use openzeppelin_stylus::proxy::utils::uups_upgradeable::UUPSUpgradeable;
307	/// use stylus_sdk::{prelude::*, storage::StorageU256};
308	///
309	/// #[storage]
310	/// #[entrypoint]
311	/// pub struct MyUpgradeableContract {
312	///     // Must include UUPSUpgradeable as the first field
313	///     uups: UUPSUpgradeable,
314	///
315	///     // Your contract's state variables
316	///     value: StorageU256,
317	///     // ...
318	/// }
319	///
320	/// #[public]
321	/// impl MyUpgradeableContract {
322	///     // Call this via the proxy once to align the proxy's version with the logic.
323	///     pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
324	///         self.uups.set_version().map_err(Into::into)
325	///     }
326	///
327	///     // Your contract's functions
328	/// }
329	/// ```
330	///
331	/// [EIP-1822]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1822
332	/// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
333	/// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
334	#[storage]
335	pub struct UUPSUpgradeable {
336	    /// Logic version number stored in the proxy contract.
337	    pub version: StorageU32}
338	
339	#[public]
340	#[implements(IUUPSUpgradeable, IErc1822Proxiable)]
341	impl UUPSUpgradeable {
342	    /// Initializes implementation-only state used for context checks.
343	    ///
344	    /// Sets `logic_flag = true` in the implementation’s storage to indicate
345	    /// a direct (non-delegated) execution context.
346	    ///
347	    /// # Arguments
348	    ///
349	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
350	    #[constructor]
351	    pub fn constructor(&mut self) {
352	        self.logic_flag().set(true);
353	    }
354	
355	    /// Sets the proxy-stored runtime `version` for this logic
356	    /// (initializer-like).
357	    ///
358	    /// Intended to be called via a proxy ([`delegate_call`][delegate_call]) to
359	    /// record `VERSION_NUMBER` in the proxy’s storage.
360	    ///
361	    /// # Arguments
362	    ///
363	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
364	    ///
365	    /// # Errors
366	    ///
367	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If not called via proxy
368	    ///   `[`delegate_call`][delegate_call]`.
369	    /// * [`Error::InvalidVersion`] - If the proxy's stored `version` is greater
370	    ///   than this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`.
371	    ///
372	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
373	    pub fn set_version(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
374	        if self.not_delegated().is_ok() {
375	            return Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(
376	                UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {},
377	            ));
378	        }
379	        if self.version.get() > VERSION_NUMBER {
380	            return Err(Error::InvalidVersion(InvalidVersion {
381	                current_version: self.version.get().to()}));
382	        }
383	
384	        self.version.set(VERSION_NUMBER);
385	        Ok(())
386	    }
387	}

393	    }

395	    #[payable]
396	    fn upgrade_to_and_call(
397	        &mut self,
398	        new_implementation: Address,
399	        data: Bytes,
400	    ) -> Result<(), Vec<u8>> {
401	        self.only_proxy()?;
402	        self._upgrade_to_and_call_uups(new_implementation, &data)?;
403

405	            UUPSUpgradeableInterface::setVersionCall {}.abi_encode();
406	        AddressUtils::function_delegate_call(
407	            self,
408	            new_implementation,
409	            &data_set_version,
410	        )?;
411	
412	        Ok(())
413	    }

417	    /// Get the logic contract version.
418	    ///
419	    /// # Arguments
420	    ///
421	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
422	    #[must_use]
423	    pub fn get_version(&self) -> U32 {
424	        VERSION_NUMBER
425	    }

427	    /// Get the logic flag from the appropriate storage slot.
428	    ///
429	    /// # Arguments
430	    ///
431	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
432	    #[must_use]
433	    pub fn logic_flag(&self) -> StorageBool {
434	        StorageSlot::get_slot::<StorageBool>(LOGIC_FLAG_SLOT)
435	    }
436	
437	    /// Return the value stored in the logic flag slot.
438	    ///
439	    /// # Arguments
440	    ///
441	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
442	    #[must_use]
443	    pub fn is_logic(&self) -> bool {
444	        self.logic_flag().get()
445	    }
446	
447	    /// Ensures the call is being made through a valid [ERC-1967] proxy.
448	    ///
449	    /// Checks:
450	    /// 1. Execution is happening via [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] (checked
451	    ///    via `!self.is_logic()`).
452	    /// 2. The caller is a valid [ERC-1967] proxy (implementation slot is
453	    ///    non-zero).
454	    /// 3. The proxy state is consistent for this logic (the proxy-stored
455	    ///    version equals this logic's `VERSION_NUMBER`).
456	    ///
457	    /// [`onlyProxy`]: https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/c64a1edb67b6e3f4a15cca8909c9482ad33a02b0/contracts/proxy/utils/UUPSUpgradeable.sol#L50
458	    ///
459	    /// # Security Implications
460	    ///
461	    /// This check prevents direct calls to upgrade functions on the
462	    /// implementation contract.
463	    ///
464	    /// Note: This is not a reentrancy guard. Use a dedicated mechanism if
465	    /// reentrancy protection is required.
466	    ///
467	    /// # Edge Cases
468	    ///
469	    /// * Calls from [ERC-1167] minimal proxies are not guaranteed to pass this
470	    ///   check
471	    ///
472	    /// # Arguments
473	    ///
474	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
475	    ///
476	    /// # Errors
477	    ///
478	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If any of the above conditions is
479	    ///   not met
480	    ///
481	    /// [ERC-1967]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1967
482	    /// [ERC-1167]: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1167
483	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
484	    pub fn only_proxy(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
485	        if self.is_logic()
486	            || Erc1967Utils::get_implementation() == Address::ZERO
487	            || U32::from(self.get_version()) != self.version.get()
488	        {
489	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
490	        } else {
491	            Ok(())
492	        }
493	    }
494	
495	    /// Check that the execution is not being performed through a
496	    /// [`delegate_call`].
497	    ///
498	    /// This allows a function to be callable on the implementing contract
499	    /// but not through proxies.
500	    ///
501	    /// # Arguments
502	    ///
503	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
504	    ///
505	    /// # Errors
506	    ///
507	    /// * [`Error::UnauthorizedCallContext`] - If the execution is performed via
508	    ///   [`delegate_call`].
509	    ///
510	    /// [`delegate_call`]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
511	    pub fn not_delegated(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
512	        if self.is_logic() {
513	            Ok(())
514	        } else {
515	            Err(Error::UnauthorizedCallContext(UUPSUnauthorizedCallContext {}))
516	        }
517	    }
518	}

529	    /// Performs an implementation upgrade with a security check for UUPS
530	    /// proxies, and additional setup call.
531	    ///
532	    /// As a security check, [`IErc1822Proxiable::proxiable_uuid`] is invoked
533	    /// in the new implementation, and the return value is expected to be the
534	    /// implementation slot in ERC-1967.
535	    ///
536	    /// # Arguments
537	    ///
538	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
539	    /// * `new_implementation` - The address of the new implementation.
540	    /// * `data` - The data to pass to the new implementation.
541	    ///
542	    /// # Errors
543	    ///
544	    /// * [`Error::InvalidImplementation`] - If the new implementation doesn't
545	    ///   support the required interface or is invalid.
546	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID`] - If the new implementation
547	    ///   returns an unsupported UUID.
548	    /// * [`Error::NonPayable`] - If the upgrade function receives ETH but is
549	    ///   not designed to handle it.
550	    /// * [`Error::EmptyCode`] - If there's no code at the new implementation
551	    ///   address.
552	    /// * [`Error::FailedCall`] - If the [`delegate_call`][delegate_call] to the
553	    ///   new implementation fails.
554	    /// * [`Error::FailedCallWithReason`] - If the
555	    ///   [`stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call`] fails with a specific reason.
556	    ///
557	    /// # Events
558	    ///
559	    /// * [`crate::proxy::erc1967::Erc1967Proxy::Upgraded`]: Emitted when the
560	    ///   implementation is upgraded.
561	    ///
562	    /// [delegate_call]: stylus_sdk::call::delegate_call
563	    fn _upgrade_to_and_call_uups(
564	        &mut self,
565	        new_implementation: Address,
566	        data: &Bytes,
567	    ) -> Result<(), Error> {
568	        let slot = Erc1822ProxiableInterface::new(new_implementation)
569	            .proxiable_uuid(Call::new_in(self))
570	            .map_err(|_e| {
571	                Error::InvalidImplementation(ERC1967InvalidImplementation {
572	                    implementation: new_implementation})
573	            })?;
574	
575	        if slot == IMPLEMENTATION_SLOT {
576	            Erc1967Utils::upgrade_to_and_call(self, new_implementation, data)
577	                .map_err(Error::from)
578	        } else {
579	            Err(Error::UnsupportedProxiableUUID(UUPSUnsupportedProxiableUUID {
580	                slot}))
581	        }
582	    }
583	}

/*!
# OpenZeppelin Contracts for Stylus

A library for secure smart contract development written in Rust for
[Arbitrum Stylus](https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/gentle-introduction).
This library offers common smart contract primitives and affordances that take
advantage of the nature of Stylus.

## Usage

To start using it, add `openzeppelin-stylus` to your `Cargo.toml`, or simply run
`cargo add openzeppelin-stylus`.

```toml
[dependencies]
openzeppelin-stylus = "x.x.x"
```

We recommend pinning to a specific version -- expect rapid iteration.

Once defined as a dependency, use one of our pre-defined implementations by
importing them:

```ignore
use openzeppelin_stylus::token::erc20::{self, Erc20, IErc20};
use stylus_sdk::{alloy_primitives::{Address, U256}, prelude::*};

#[entrypoint]
#[storage]
struct MyContract {
    pub erc20: Erc20}

#[public]
#[implements(IErc20<Error = erc20::Error>)]
impl MyContract {}

#[public]
impl IErc20 for MyContract {
    type Error = erc20::Error;

    fn total_supply(&self) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.total_supply()
    }

    fn balance_of(&self, account: Address) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.balance_of(account)
    }

    fn transfer(
        &mut self,
        to: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.transfer(to, value)
    }

    fn allowance(&self, owner: Address, spender: Address) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.allowance(owner, spender)
    }

    fn approve(
        &mut self,
        spender: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.approve(spender, value)
    }

    fn transfer_from(
        &mut self,
        from: Address,
        to: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.transfer_from(from, to, value)
    }
}
```
*/

#![allow(
    clippy::module_name_repetitions,
    clippy::used_underscore_items,
    clippy::unreadable_literal,
    deprecated
)]
#![cfg_attr(not(any(test, feature = "export-abi")), no_std, no_main)]
#![cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, feature(coverage_attribute))]
#![deny(rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links)]
extern crate alloc;

pub mod access;
pub mod finance;
pub mod proxy;
pub mod token;
pub mod utils;

#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) mod test_utils;

[package]
name = "openzeppelin-stylus"
description = "OpenZeppelin Contracts for Stylus"
edition.workspace = true
categories = ["cryptography::cryptocurrencies", "no-std", "wasm"]
keywords = ["arbitrum", "ethereum", "stylus", "smart-contracts", "standards"]
license.workspace = true
repository.workspace = true
version.workspace = true

[dependencies]
alloy-primitives.workspace = true
alloy-sol-types.workspace = true
alloy-sol-macro.workspace = true
stylus-sdk.workspace = true
keccak-const.workspace = true
openzeppelin-stylus-proc.workspace = true

[dev-dependencies]
alloy-primitives = { workspace = true, features = ["arbitrary"] }
stylus-sdk = { workspace = true, features = ["stylus-test"] }

[features]
reentrant = ["stylus-sdk/reentrant"]
export-abi = ["stylus-sdk/export-abi"]

[lib]
crate-type = ["lib"]

[lints]
workspace = true

members = [
  "benches",
  "contracts",

]
