]
exclude = ["fuzz", "templates/crypto-erc20"]

# Explicitly set the resolver to version 2, which is the default for packages
# with edition >= 2021.
# https://doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/rust-2021/default-cargo-resolver.html
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
authors = ["OpenZeppelin"]
edition = "2021"
license = "MIT"
repository = "https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/rust-contracts-stylus"
version = "0.3.0"

[workspace.lints.rust]
missing_docs = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"
rust_2021_compatibility = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
unexpected_cfgs = { level = "warn", check-cfg = ['cfg(coverage_nightly)'] }

[workspace.lints.clippy]
pedantic = "warn"
all = "warn"

[workspace.dependencies]
# Stylus SDK related
stylus-sdk = "=0.10.10"
# Devnet tooling used by the end-to-end tests and benches (dev-only).
stylus-tools = { version = "=0.10.10", features = ["integration-tests"] }

# `alloy` is used by the end-to-end tests and benches. The contracts only depend
# on `alloy-primitives` and `alloy-sol-types`, which must match the versions the
# Stylus SDK is built against.
alloy = { version = "=1.7.3", features = ["essentials", "signer-local"] }
alloy-primitives = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false, features = [
  "tiny-keccak",
] }
alloy-sol-types = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false }
alloy-sol-macro = { version = "=1.5.7", default-features = false }

ruint = "^1.17.1"

eyre = "0.6.8"
keccak-const = "0.2.0"
rand = "0.9.0"
regex = "1.10.4"
tiny-keccak = { version = "2.0.2", features = ["keccak"] }
tokio = { version = "1.45", features = ["full"] }
futures = "0.3.30"
num-traits = "0.2.14"
zeroize = { version = "1.8.1", features = ["derive"] }
proptest = "1"
educe = "0.6.0"
hex-literal = "0.4.1"
sha2 = "0.10.9"
static_assertions = "1.1.0"

# procedural macros
syn = { version = "2.0.58", features = ["full"] }
proc-macro2 = "1.0.79"
quote = "1.0.35"

# members
e2e = { path = "lib/e2e" }
e2e-proc = { path = "lib/e2e-proc" }
openzeppelin-stylus = { path = "contracts" }
openzeppelin-stylus-proc = { path = "contracts-proc", version = "=0.3.0" }
openzeppelin-crypto = { path = "lib/crypto" }

[profile.release]
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
opt-level = "z"
strip = true
lto = true
debug = false
rpath = false
debug-assertions = false
incremental = false

[profile.dev]
panic = "abort"

[workspace.metadata.typos]
default = { extend-ignore-identifiers-re = [
  # ignore hex data samples.
  "[0-9a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F]",
] }
files = { extend-exclude = [] }
[toolchain]
channel = "1.91.0"
components = ["rustfmt", "clippy", "rust-src"]
targets = ["wasm32-unknown-unknown"]
max_width = 80
format_macro_matchers = true
group_imports = "StdExternalCrate"
imports_granularity = "Crate"
reorder_impl_items = true
use_field_init_shorthand = true
use_small_heuristics = "Max"
wrap_comments = true

openzeppelin-stylus = "x.x.x"

Once defined as a dependency, use one of our pre-defined implementations by
importing them:

```ignore
use openzeppelin_stylus::token::erc20::{self, Erc20, IErc20};
use stylus_sdk::{alloy_primitives::{Address, U256}, prelude::*};

#[entrypoint]
#[storage]
struct MyContract {
    pub erc20: Erc20}

#[public]
#[implements(IErc20<Error = erc20::Error>)]
impl MyContract {}

#[public]
impl IErc20 for MyContract {
    type Error = erc20::Error;

    fn total_supply(&self) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.total_supply()
    }

    fn balance_of(&self, account: Address) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.balance_of(account)
    }

    fn transfer(
        &mut self,
        to: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.transfer(to, value)
    }

    fn allowance(&self, owner: Address, spender: Address) -> U256 {
        self.erc20.allowance(owner, spender)
    }

    fn approve(
        &mut self,
        spender: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.approve(spender, value)
    }

    fn transfer_from(
        &mut self,
        from: Address,
        to: Address,
        value: U256,
    ) -> Result<bool, Self::Error> {
        self.erc20.transfer_from(from, to, value)
    }
}
```

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

#!/bin/zsh
# Builds an isolated crate (outside the repo worktrees) holding the proxy module
# plus the minimal set of other modules it depends on, so that the proxy unit
# tests can be compiled and run before the whole crate compiles.
set -euo pipefail
W=/tmp/bench/wt/proxy
S=/tmp/bench/scratch-proxy/ws
rm -rf "$S"
mkdir -p "$S/contracts/src"
cp "$W/Cargo.lock" "$W/rust-toolchain.toml" "$W/rustfmt.toml" "$W/clippy.toml" "$S/"
cp -R "$W/contracts-proc" "$S/contracts-proc"
rm -rf "$S/contracts-proc/target"
# workspace manifest limited to the two crates
python3 -I - "$W/Cargo.toml" "$S/Cargo.toml" <<'PY'
import re, sys
src = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
src = re.sub(r'\[workspace\]\nmembers = \[.*?\]\n\ndefault-members = \[.*?\]\n',
             '[workspace]\nmembers = ["contracts", "contracts-proc"]\n', src, flags=re.S)
open(sys.argv[2], 'w').write(src)
PY
cp "$W/contracts/Cargo.toml" "$S/contracts/Cargo.toml"
C="$W/contracts/src"
D="$S/contracts/src"
mkdir -p "$D/utils/introspection" "$D/utils/math" "$D/access" "$D/token/erc20"
strip_tests() { # drop the trailing #[cfg(test)] module of a copied file
  python3 -I - "$1" <<'PY'
import re, sys
p = sys.argv[1]
t = open(p).read()
m = re.search(r'^#\[cfg\(test\)\]\n', t, flags=re.M)
if m:
    t = t[:m.start()]
open(p, 'w').write(t)
PY
}
cp "$C/test_utils.rs" "$D/test_utils.rs"
cp "$C/utils/address.rs" "$D/utils/address.rs"; strip_tests "$D/utils/address.rs"
cp "$C/utils/storage_slot.rs" "$D/utils/storage_slot.rs"; strip_tests "$D/utils/storage_slot.rs"
cp "$C/utils/introspection/mod.rs" "$D/utils/introspection/mod.rs"
cp "$C/utils/introspection/erc165.rs" "$D/utils/introspection/erc165.rs"; strip_tests "$D/utils/introspection/erc165.rs"
cp -R "$C/utils/math/." "$D/utils/math/"
for f in $(find "$D/utils/math" -name '*.rs'); do strip_tests "$f"; done
cp "$C/access/ownable.rs" "$D/access/ownable.rs"; strip_tests "$D/access/ownable.rs"
cp "$C/token/erc20/mod.rs" "$D/token/erc20/mod.rs"; strip_tests "$D/token/erc20/mod.rs"
sed -i '' -e '/^pub mod extensions;$/d' -e '/^pub mod interface;$/d' -e '/^pub mod utils;$/d' "$D/token/erc20/mod.rs"
cat > "$D/utils/mod.rs" <<'RS'
//! Reduced utils for the isolated proxy test crate.
pub mod address;
pub mod introspection;
pub mod math;
pub mod storage_slot;
RS
cat > "$D/access/mod.rs" <<'RS'
//! Reduced access for the isolated proxy test crate.
pub mod ownable;
RS
cat > "$D/token/mod.rs" <<'RS'
//! Reduced token for the isolated proxy test crate.
pub mod erc20;
RS
python3 -I - "$C/lib.rs" "$D/lib.rs" <<'PY'
import sys
t = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
t = t.replace('pub mod finance;\n', '').replace('pub mod access;', 'pub mod access;')
open(sys.argv[2], 'w').write(t)
PY
echo "scratch crate prepared in $S"
EOF

content.content:
name: check
# This workflow runs whenever a PR is opened or updated, or a commit is pushed
# to main. It runs several checks:
# - fmt: checks that the code is formatted according to `rustfmt`.
# - clippy: checks that the code does not contain any `clippy` warnings.
# - doc: checks that the code can be documented without errors.
# - hack: check combinations of feature flags.
# - typos: checks for typos across the repo.
permissions:
  contents: read
# This configuration allows maintainers of this repo to create a branch and
# pull request based on the new branch. Restricting the push trigger to the
# main branch ensures that the PR only gets built once.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, v*]
  pull_request:
# If new code is pushed to a PR branch, then cancel in progress workflows for
# that PR. Ensures that we don't waste CI time, and returns results quicker.
# https://github.com/jonhoo/rust-ci-conf/pull/5
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
jobs:
  fmt:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: nightly / fmt
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: true

      - name: Install rust
        # We run in nightly to make use of some features only available there.
        # Check out `rustfmt.toml` to see which ones.
        uses: actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@v1
        with:
          toolchain: nightly-2025-08-01
          components: rustfmt
          rustflags: ""

      - name: Check formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all --check

  clippy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: ${{ matrix.toolchain }} / clippy
    permissions:
      contents: read
      checks: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Get early warning of new lints which are regularly introduced in beta
        # channels.
        toolchain: [stable, beta]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: true

      - name: Install rust ${{ matrix.toolchain }}
        uses: actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@v1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ matrix.toolchain }}
          components: clippy
          rustflags: ""

      - name: Cargo clippy
        uses: giraffate/clippy-action@v1
        with:
          reporter: "github-pr-check"
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          clippy_flags: --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings -D clippy::all -D clippy::pedantic
  doc:
    # Run docs generation on nightly rather than stable. This enables features
    # like https://doc.rust-lang.org/beta/unstable-book/language-features/doc-cfg.html
    # which allows an API be documented as only available in some specific
    # platforms.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: nightly / doc
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: true

      - name: Install rust
        uses: actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@v1
        with:
          toolchain: nightly-2025-08-01
          rustflags: ""

      - name: Cargo doc
        run: cargo doc --no-deps --all-features
        env:
          RUSTDOCFLAGS: --cfg docsrs

  hack:
    # `cargo-hack` checks combinations of feature flags to ensure that features
    # are all additive which is required for feature unification.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: ubuntu / stable / features
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: true

      - name: Install rust
        uses: actions-rust-lang/setup-rust-toolchain@v1
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          target: wasm32-unknown-unknown
          rustflags: ""

      - name: Cargo install cargo-hack
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@cargo-hack
        # Intentionally no target specifier; see https://github.com/jonhoo/rust-ci-conf/pull/4
        # `--feature-powerset` runs for every combination of features. Note that
        # target in this context means one of `--lib`, `--bin`, etc, and not the
        # target triple.
      - name: Cargo hack
        run: cargo hack check --feature-powerset --depth 2 --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --workspace --exclude e2e --exclude basic-script-example --exclude benches

  typos:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: ubuntu / stable / typos
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Actions Repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check spelling of files in the workspace
        uses: crate-ci/typos@v1

  nostd:
    # This job checks whether the library is able to run without the std
    # library.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: ${{ matrix.target }}

56:        run: cargo generate-lockfile

62:        # https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/6669

1	//! This is a low-level set of contracts implementing different proxy patterns
2	//! with and without upgradeability.
3	use alloc::vec::Vec;
4	
5	use alloy_primitives::Address;
6	use stylus_sdk::{call, prelude::*, stylus_core::calls::errors::Error};
7	
8	pub mod beacon;
9	pub mod erc1967;
10	pub mod utils;
11	
12	/// This trait provides a fallback function that delegates all calls to another
13	/// contract using the Stylus [`delegate_call`] function. We
14	/// refer to the second contract as the _implementation_ behind the proxy, and
15	/// it has to be specified by overriding the virtual [`IProxy::implementation`]
16	/// function.
17	///
18	/// Additionally, delegation to the implementation can be triggered manually
19	/// through the [`IProxy::do_fallback`] function, or to a different contract
20	/// through the [`IProxy::delegate`] function.
21	///
22	/// The success and return data of the delegated call will be returned back
23	/// to the caller of the proxy.
24	///
25	/// The proxy reaches the host environment through [`HostAccess::vm`], which is
26	/// why implementors have to be [`HostAccess`] (every `#[storage]` type is).
27	///
28	/// # Safety
29	///
30	/// This trait is unsafe to implement because it uses the `unsafe`
31	/// [`delegate_call`] function.
32	///
33	/// The caller must ensure that `self` is a valid contract storage context.
34	///
35	/// The caller must ensure that the implementation contract is a valid contract
36	/// address.
37	pub unsafe trait IProxy: TopLevelStorage + HostAccess + Sized {
38	    /// Delegates the current call to [`IProxy::implementation`].
39	    ///
40	    /// This function does not return to its internal call site, it will
41	    /// return directly to the external caller.
42	    ///
43	    /// # Arguments
44	    ///
45	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
46	    /// * `implementation` - The address of the implementation contract.
47	    /// * `calldata` - The calldata to delegate to the implementation contract.
48	    ///
49	    /// # Errors
50	    ///
51	    /// Returns a [`stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error`] if the
52	    /// delegate call fails. This error may represent:
53	    /// * A revert from the implementation contract, containing the revert data.
54	    /// * Failure to decode the return data from the implementation contract.
55	    /// * Other low-level call failures as defined by the Stylus SDK.
56	    #[allow(clippy::missing_safety_doc)]
57	    unsafe fn delegate(
58	        &mut self,
59	        implementation: Address,
60	        calldata: &[u8],
61	    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error> {
62	        // `Call::new_mutating` only needs `self` to prove exclusive access to
63	        // the top-level storage. Its borrow ends right away, which lets
64	        // `self.vm()` be borrowed for the call itself.
65	        let call = Call::new_mutating(self);
66	        call::delegate_call(self.vm(), call, implementation, calldata)
67	    }
68	
69	    /// This is a virtual function that should be overridden so it
70	    /// returns the address to which the fallback function and
71	    /// [`IProxy::do_fallback`] should delegate.
72	    ///
73	    /// # Arguments
74	    ///
75	    /// * `&self` - Read access to the contract's state.
76	    ///
77	    /// # Errors
78	    ///
79	    /// Implementing contracts should define their own error types for this
80	    /// function. Typically, errors may include:
81	    /// * The implementation address is invalid (e.g., not a contract).
82	    /// * The implementation is not a contract.
83	    ///
84	    /// The error should be encoded as a `Vec<u8>`.
85	    fn implementation(&self) -> Result<Address, Vec<u8>>;
86	
87	    /// Fallback function that delegates calls to the address returned
88	    /// by [`IProxy::implementation`]. Will run if no other function in the
89	    /// contract matches the call data.
90	    ///
91	    /// # Arguments
92	    ///
93	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
94	    /// * `calldata` - The calldata to delegate to the implementation contract.
95	    ///
96	    /// # Errors
97	    ///
98	    /// Implementing contracts should define their own error types for this
99	    /// function. Typically, errors may include:
100	    /// * The implementation address is invalid (e.g., not a contract).
101	    /// * The implementation is not a contract.
102	    /// * The implementation reverted with a reason.
103	    ///
104	    /// The error should be encoded as a `Vec<u8>`.
105	    #[allow(clippy::missing_safety_doc)]
106	    unsafe fn do_fallback(
107	        &mut self,
108	        calldata: &[u8],
109	    ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>> {
110	        Ok(self.delegate(self.implementation()?, calldata)?)
111	    }
112	}
113	
114	// The unit tests of the proxies are not built with the `export-abi` feature.
115	// For the ABI export, `#[public]` defines items at the level of the module
116	// (like `print_from_args`), that collide as soon as a module defines several
117	// contracts, as the tests of the proxies do. They have no use for the export.
118	
119	/// Helpers shared by the unit tests of the proxies.
120	///
121	/// [`TestVM`](stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM) holds the state of a single contract
122	/// and doesn't run the contracts a call is made to: the outcome of such a call
123	/// is whatever has been mocked for it. The helpers run those contracts, so that
124	/// their outcome can be mocked.
125	#[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "export-abi")))]
126	mod test_helpers {
127	    use core::{borrow::BorrowMut, fmt::Debug};
128	
129	    use alloy_primitives::Address;
130	    use alloy_sol_types::SolEvent;
131	    use stylus_sdk::{
132	        abi::{router_entrypoint, Router},
133	        host::VM,
134	        prelude::*,
135	        testing::TestVM,
136	        ArbResult,
137	    };
138	
139	    /// Gives some code to `account`, so that `vm` sees a contract there.
140	    pub(crate) fn deploy(vm: &TestVM, account: Address) {
141	        vm.set_code(account, vec![0x60, 0x00]);
142	    }
143	
144	    /// Runs `calldata` on the contract `C` over the state held by `vm`, the
145	    /// way the contract's entrypoint does.
146	    ///
147	    /// A delegate call runs the code of the callee over the storage of the
148	    /// caller, so the outcome of a delegate call is the one of running the
149	    /// callee over the state of the caller's `vm`. The state changes and the
150	    /// logs of the callee end up in `vm` as well.
151	    pub(crate) fn execute<C>(vm: &TestVM, calldata: &[u8]) -> ArbResult
152	    where
153	        C: Router<C>
154	            + StorageType
155	            + TopLevelStorage
156	            + ValueDenier
157	            + BorrowMut<<C as Router<C>>::Storage>,
158	    {
159	        router_entrypoint::<C, C>(
160	            calldata.to_vec(),
161	            VM { host: Box::new(vm.clone()) },
162	        )
163	    }
164	
165	    /// Asserts that `event` was emitted at least once.
166	    #[track_caller]
167	    pub(crate) fn assert_emitted<E: SolEvent + Debug>(vm: &TestVM, event: &E) {
168	        let log = event.encode_log_data();
169	        let expected = (log.topics().to_vec(), log.data.to_vec());
170	        let emitted = vm.get_emitted_logs();
171	        assert!(
172	            emitted.contains(&expected),
173	            "event was not emitted: {event:?}, emitted logs: {emitted:?}"
174	        );
175	    }
176	}
177	
178	// Not built with `export-abi`, see `proxy::test_helpers`.
179	#[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "export-abi")))]
180	mod tests {
181	    use alloy_sol_macro::sol;
182	    use alloy_sol_types::{SolCall, SolError, SolValue};
183	    use stylus_sdk::{
184	        alloy_primitives::{address, Address, U256},
185	        prelude::*,
186	        storage::{StorageAddress, StorageBool},
187	        testing::TestVM,
188	        ArbResult,
189	    };

194	        test_utils::{ALICE, BOB},
195	        token::erc20::{self, Erc20, IErc20},
196	    };

refactor(proxy): use the VM host access of Stylus SDK 0.10

The proxy contracts still used the SDK 0.9 helpers that were removed in the
base commit. `IProxy::delegate` builds its call context with
`Call::new_mutating` before borrowing `self.vm()`, so the trait now requires
`HostAccess`. The beacon and `proxiable_uuid` lookups pass the VM and a static
`Call::new()` to their `sol_interface!` wrappers, `UpgradeableBeacon` checks
the code of the implementation with `AddressUtils::has_code`, and the
`Erc1967Utils` and `StorageSlot` getters get the contract as their context.

The public interface traits opt out of `missing_docs`, which the `#[public]`
macro triggers with an undocumented helper method. The rustdoc that pointed at
`msg::value` (the link no longer resolves) now names `msg_value()` through the
VM, a broken link to the `Upgraded` event is fixed, and the `delegate_call`
links that the new prelude makes redundant are simplified. The files are
formatted again.

test(proxy): run the IProxy unit tests on the Stylus TestVM

Replace motsu with `TestVM`. The delegate calls of the proxy are mocked, so the
tests share a few helpers: `execute` runs a contract through its router over
the state of a `TestVM`, which is what the EVM does for a delegate call and
lets the mocks carry the real outcome of the implementation, `deploy` gives
code to an account, and `assert_emitted` looks for an event in the logs.

Because the implementation runs in the context of the proxy, the `Transfer`
events are now asserted on the proxy, which the old tests could not do. The
second implementation of `direct_delegate_to_different_implementation` reads
the storage of the proxy, and the proxy is configured with an implementation
that would fail, to prove that the given address is the one that is called.

The tests are not built with the `export-abi` feature, for which the
`#[public]` macro defines module level items that collide when a module has
several contracts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

test(proxy): run the ERC-1967 unit tests on the Stylus TestVM

Replace motsu with `TestVM`. The delegate calls to the implementation run it
over the state of the contract, and a beacon is a contract that answers
`implementation()` with the address it holds, mocked as a static call.

`TestVM` answers every call with the return data of the last mock registered,
whichever call it is for. Upgrading to a beacon with setup data asks the beacon
for the implementation and delegates the data to it, so the beacon is mocked
last and the two tests where the setup call fails (it reverts with the encoded
address of the implementation instead of the reason the old tests used, which
was a motsu message) check that the revert data of the delegate call is
returned unchanged.

`upgrade_beacon_to_and_call_with_beacon_returning_invalid_implementation` stays
ignored: `TestVM` doesn't roll back the storage writes of a call that fails, so
the beacon slot written before the check stays set. The reason of the ignore
no longer mentions motsu.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
The proxy module is migrated to SDK 0.10.10 on `agent/proxy`, and all 61 tests are converted to `TestVM`. In an isolated export of merged `bench` + `agent/erc20` + this branch, 60 proxy tests pass and 1 is ignored.

**Files** are the 8 under `contracts/src/proxy/**`: `mod.rs`, `beacon/{mod,proxy,upgradeable}.rs`, `erc1967/{mod,utils}.rs`, `utils/{erc1822,uups_upgradeable}.rs`. There are no manifest changes and no `contract-client-gen` feature.

**Commits** (`git log --oneline 7e36233..HEAD`):
- `dfc88b2` refactor(proxy): require the VM as the host of IProxy
- `acc3a3a` test(proxy): run the UUPS unit tests on the Stylus TestVM
- `75873d4` test(proxy): run the beacon unit tests on the Stylus TestVM
- `f6ff26e` test(proxy): run the ERC-1967 unit tests on the Stylus TestVM
- `43b509a` test(proxy): run the IProxy unit tests on the Stylus TestVM
- `1924324` refactor(proxy): use the VM host access of Stylus SDK 0.10

**Signature changes**
- `IProxy` supertraits go from `TopLevelStorage + Sized` to `TopLevelStorage + HostAccess<Host = VM> + Sized`. `delegate` and `do_fallback` stay `unsafe fn` with their safety docs. `IProxy` is not tagged `#[public]`, since that would add `implementation()` to every proxy's ABI.
- The generated `IBeaconInterface::implementation` and `Erc1822ProxiableInterface::proxiable_uuid` go from `f(ctx)` to `f(host, ctx)`. Call sites use `self.vm()` and `Call::new()`.
- The `Erc1967Utils` getters and `change_admin` take `context` first, as the base commit already did; I completed their docs. The private `get_beacon_implementation` now takes `&impl HostAccess<Host = VM>`.
- `IBeacon`, `IErc1822Proxiable`, `IUpgradeableBeacon` and `IUUPSUpgradeable` carry `#[public]` plus `#[allow(missing_docs)]` with a one-line reason. No `Self::Error` is left in my files.

**Test inventory** (`#[test]` before and after): `mod.rs` 5/5, `erc1967/mod.rs` 4/4, `erc1967/utils.rs` 26/26, `beacon/proxy.rs` 4/4, `beacon/upgradeable.rs` 17/17, `uups_upgradeable.rs` 5/5. Names are identical and none were merged or removed.
- **Delegate emulation:** `test_helpers::execute` (in `proxy/mod.rs`) runs the implementation's router over the proxy's `TestVM`, and the result is mocked. Transfer events are now asserted on the proxy, which resolves the old TODOs.
- **UUPS:** `constructs` and `fallback` were `#[ignore]`d for motsu. They now run and pass.
- **Still ignored:** `upgrade_beacon_to_and_call_with_beacon_returning_invalid_implementation`. `TestVM` never rolls back storage on a failed call. The reason text no longer mentions motsu.
- **Single return buffer:** every `TestVM` call returns the data of the last mock registered, matched or not. Three tests keep their scenario but the revert data is the ABI-encoded beacon answer instead of the old data:
  - `beacon::proxy::fallback_returns_error`
  - `erc1967::utils::upgrade_beacon_to_and_call_with_delegate_call_failure`
  - `erc1967::utils::upgrade_beacon_to_and_call_with_beacon_implementation_reverts`

  Success paths through `BeaconProxy.fallback` cannot prove which target was delegated to.
- `upgrade_to_and_call_with_delegate_call_failure` now mocks the old motsu reason text; the expected value is unchanged.
- `direct_delegate_to_different_implementation` seeds the proxy's storage, because a delegate call reads it, and adds an `Err` decoy mock for the stored implementation.
- **Export-abi gate:** test modules use `#[cfg(all(test, not(feature = "export-abi")))]`. The SDK 0.10 `#[public]` macro emits module-level items that collide when a module defines several contracts.

**Compile status**
- In the worktree: 0 errors in my files for lib and tests. The whole crate at the base commit still fails from other modules.
- Isolated export (`/tmp/bench/scratch-proxy/integ`, outside the worktrees; logs `/tmp/bench/logs/proxy-integ-*.log`):
  - `cargo test --lib` gives 632 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored (1 mine).
  - `clippy --all-targets -D warnings -D clippy::pedantic` gives 0 diagnostics.
  - `cargo doc` gives 0 diagnostics, doctests pass, and the wasm32 release check passes.
- A dry-run `git merge-tree` of `agent/proxy` into `bench` is clean. `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01` is clean on my files.

**Requests**
- `examples/erc1967-invalid/src/lib.rs:40`: `data.as_slice()` is private in alloy 1.6, use `as_ref()`.
- `examples/uups-proxy-new-version/src/lib.rs`: it needs the same call-site fixes as `uups_upgradeable.rs` (`get_slot(context, ..)`, `get_implementation(self)`, `proxiable_uuid(self.vm(), Call::new())`, and drop the `call::Call` import).
- `Self::Error` in public trait impls breaks `--all-features` with 14 E0220 errors. Affected: `access/control/{mod,extensions/enumerable}.rs`, `access/ownable_two_step.rs`, `finance/vesting_wallet.rs`, and `examples/uups-proxy*`.
- Nothing else is blocked.
